A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same StyleGuard study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A and B are readable and support comparison, including the checklist added in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on style mimicry and identity personalization, including quantitative comparisons in Tables 1–5 and human evaluations in Figure 4 and Appendix A.7.

after.justification: v2 retains these original quantitative and human-evaluation results and includes revised qualitative outputs in Figure 11.

M1.justification: Equation (8) changes the protected-image PGD update from adding to subtracting the signed gradient of the StyleGuard loss. This corrects a stated algorithm step; the losses, model ensembles, and alternating optimization remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether implementation code changed or experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate WikiArt style mimicry and CelebA identity personalization. DreamBooth, Textual Inversion, and the same transformation, DiffPure, Noise Upscaling, and online FIE scenarios are retained; Appendix B introduces no new coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: Glaze, Mist, Anti-DreamBooth, MetaCloak, and SimAC in Tables 1 and 4; Anti-DreamBooth in Table 2; and Anti-DreamBooth, MetaCloak, and SimAC in Tables 3 and 5.

E3.justification: The detailed evaluation protocols remain unchanged, including the 40-artist and 100-identity samples, training/evaluation splits, generated-image counts, model configurations, perturbation budgets, and five-annotator evaluation. No changed experimental settings accompany the replacement Figure 11 samples.

E4.justification: Appendix B revises its qualitative comparison of mimicry from clean versus protected paintings by replacing the protected-output examples in Figure 11. The loss ablations and other robustness, transferability, and personalization analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 4's distribution displays and the five-annotator protocol are unchanged. The new checklist asserts that statistical significance was evaluated but supplies no new test, uncertainty estimate, error-bar definition, or run/seed information.

E6.justification: Figure 11 contains different generated-image examples, changing the reported qualitative results. All numerical entries in Tables 1–5 are unchanged; for example, Table 1 retains StyleGuard's Noise Upscaling FID of 401.80 and precision of 0.00. The replacement images do not establish a performance gain.

T1.justification: The sign correction in Equation (8) changes the formal update from gradient ascent to descent, making it consistent with the style objective and negative denoising-error losses. The remaining mathematical formulation is retained, with no added assumptions, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The introduction removes the contribution bullet's claim to be the 'first robust method' and emphasizes protection against DreamBooth with attacker preprocessing. The abstract and conclusion retain the broader claims about transferability, purification robustness, Textual Inversion, and identity protection.

C2.justification: The explanations involving global style features, LoRA adaptation, and FIE denoising remain substantively unchanged. Section 6 retains the limitations concerning commercial upscalers and LoRA-based fine-tuning; the checklist adds no substantive scientific qualification.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link in the abstract and a code-availability statement in the checklist. The implementation settings, hardware, and runtime information in the technical appendices are retained. Repository contents and accessibility cannot be verified from the PDFs alone.

R1.justification: Removing the introduction's 'first robust method' claim modestly softens the novelty positioning. The cited works and substantive comparisons with prior research remain the same; conversion to numbered references does not add literature.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized introduction, background, and contribution-list edits, updates the affiliation and conference heading, adopts numbered citations, and adds an acknowledgment and NeurIPS checklist. The scientific section sequence and most prose remain intact. Appendix B also introduces an erroneous repeated reference to Figure 10.

P2.justification: Figures 9 and 10 reproduce the same examples at higher resolution, while Figure 11 replaces its image montage. Figure placement and surrounding page layout change, including moving Figure 4 upward on page 8. The other figure content and all table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Correcting Equation (8) resolves an implementation-relevant inconsistency between the update direction and the stated losses, while the new code pointer improves reproducibility information. These provide a limited net gain without stronger quantitative evidence. The gain is tempered by reporting defects: the added checklist denies human-subject research despite the retained five-annotator study in Appendix A.7.
